no: See Kadir Altintas and Ercole Suppa, `Hyacinthos 28982 <http://www.hyacinthos.epizy.com/message.php?msg=28982>`__.

Let (P_{A}) be the pedal circle of the A-vertex of the anticomplementary triangle (and of the A-vertex of the tangential triangle), and define (P_{B}) and (P_{C}) cyclically. Let \(R_{A}\) be the radical center of (O), (P_{B}), (P_{C}) (where (O) is the circumcircle). Define \(R_{B}\) and \(R_{C}\) cyclically. The lines \(AR_{A}\), \(BR_{B}\), \(CR_{C}\) concur in X_32085. (Randy Hutson, June 7, 2019)

Generalization: Let X = \(x : y : z\) and X' = \(1/x : 1/y : 1/z\) (trilinears) be two isogonal conjugate points. Let (P_{A}) be the pedal circle of the A-vertex of the anticevian triangle of X (and of the A-vertex of the anticevian triangle of X'), and define (P_{B}) and (P_{C}) cyclically. Let \(R_{A}\) be the radical center of (O), (P_{B}), (P_{C}). Define \(R_{B}\) and \(R_{C}\) cyclically. The lines \(AR_{A}\), \(BR_{B}\), \(CR_{C}\) concur in the polar conjugate of the isotomic conjugate of the cevapoint of X and X', with trilinears 1/(x (y^2 + z^2) (a^2 - b^2 - c^2)) : :. (Randy Hutson, June 7, 2019)
